patterns.description: The cardholder's bank account does not have enough balance to cover the transaction amount.
patterns.rootCause: The issuing bank's authorization system returned response code 51 (insufficient funds). Common around month-end or before salary credit dates in India.
recommendedActions: Wait 24 hours for potential salary/credit cycle replenishment
Send gentle nudge suggesting alternate payment method (UPI, another card)
If recurring subscription, initiate dunning sequence with 3 retry attempts over 72 hours
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI Circular CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-516 mandates maximum 3 auto-debit retry attempts within 24 hours

patterns.description: The issuing bank's fraud detection system flagged and rejected this transaction as potentially risky.
patterns.rootCause: The card issuer's risk engine detected anomalous patterns such as unusual transaction amount, unfamiliar merchant category, or geographic mismatch. This is an automated bank-side decision.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry immediately — repeated attempts will increase risk score
Send customer a message asking them to whitelist the merchant with their bank
Suggest an alternate payment method (UPI or net banking) to bypass card risk engine

patterns.description: The card used for the transaction has passed its expiry date and is no longer valid for transactions.
patterns.rootCause: The card's expiry date (MM/YY) has passed. The issuing bank rejects all transactions on expired cards with response code 54.
recommendedActions: Send customer notification to update their card details
Provide direct link to payment method update page
If subscription, pause billing and send renewal reminder

patterns.description: The card has been reported as lost or stolen by the cardholder to the issuing bank.
patterns.rootCause: The issuing bank has flagged this card in the hot list (response code 43). All transactions will be declined until a replacement card is issued.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry — this card is permanently blocked
Send customer a notification about the declined payment
Request customer to update with a new card or use alternate payment method

patterns.description: The transaction amount exceeds the card's daily, weekly, or monthly spending limit set by the bank or cardholder.
patterns.rootCause: Most Indian banks impose default transaction limits (e.g., ₹2L/day for debit cards, ₹5L/day for credit cards). The cardholder may also have set custom lower limits via mobile banking.
recommendedActions: Wait 24 hours for daily limit reset
Send nudge suggesting customer increase their card limit via bank app
Offer to split the payment into smaller installments or EMI
Suggest alternate payment method (UPI has separate limits)
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates banks to allow customers to set their own per-transaction and daily limits for debit cards

patterns.description: The card number entered by the customer is incorrect or does not pass the Luhn checksum validation.
patterns.rootCause: The customer likely mistyped one or more digits of their card number. The Luhn algorithm check failed at the gateway level before even reaching the bank.
recommendedActions: Show clear error message asking customer to re-enter card details
Implement auto-formatting and Luhn validation on the frontend
Offer saved card tokenization for repeat customers
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI Card-on-File Tokenization guidelines (2022) — merchants must tokenize cards via certified token requestors

patterns.description: A generic decline from the issuing bank without a specific reason. The bank chose not to honor this transaction.
patterns.rootCause: Response code 05 (Do Not Honor) is a catch-all decline used when the bank's internal systems reject the transaction for undisclosed reasons. Could be temporary holds, internal risk flags, or system issues.
recommendedActions: Wait 4 hours and retry once
If retry fails, send customer a nudge to contact their bank
Suggest alternate payment method as fallback

patterns.description: The card has been restricted by the issuing bank for certain types of transactions or merchant categories.
patterns.rootCause: The bank has restricted this card from e-commerce or international transactions. Common with corporate cards or newly issued cards in India that require activation for online use.
recommendedActions: Send customer notification to enable online transactions via bank app
Suggest alternate payment method (UPI, net banking)
Do not retry with the same card until customer confirms activation
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates banks to allow customers to enable/disable domestic and international e-commerce transactions

patterns.description: The acquiring bank did not respond to the payment gateway within the expected time window.
patterns.rootCause: The payment request timed out between the gateway and the acquiring bank's servers. Often caused by high transaction volume during peak hours (flash sales, festival seasons) or transient network congestion.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately through the same gateway
If immediate retry fails, switch to an alternate payment gateway
Monitor gateway health dashboard for systemic issues

patterns.description: The payment processor is experiencing a full or partial outage and is unable to process transactions.
patterns.rootCause: The upstream payment processor (e.g., NPCI for UPI, Visa/Mastercard for cards) is experiencing downtime. These outages are typically short (5-30 minutes) but affect all merchants on that processor.
recommendedActions: Immediately route transactions through an alternate gateway/processor
If no alternate gateway, queue the transaction for retry in 5 minutes
Send proactive status update to the customer about the temporary issue

patterns.description: A network connectivity issue occurred between the payment gateway and the banking network.
patterns.rootCause: TCP/TLS connection failure or DNS resolution error between the payment gateway's servers and the bank's API endpoints. Can be caused by ISP issues, CDN failures, or firewall rule changes.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — network errors are usually transient
If second attempt fails, switch to a different gateway with a separate network path
Log the error for infrastructure team review

patterns.description: The payment gateway has rate-limited the merchant due to exceeding API request limits.
patterns.rootCause: The merchant exceeded the gateway's API rate limit (e.g., Razorpay allows 25 requests/second per API key). Commonly triggered during flash sales or batch processing.
recommendedActions: Implement exponential backoff — wait 1 minute before retrying
Contact gateway provider to increase rate limits
Distribute traffic across multiple API keys or gateway accounts

patterns.description: The payment was authorized but the settlement process between banks failed to complete.
patterns.rootCause: The settlement batch between the acquiring and issuing banks failed during the daily settlement cycle. The funds are held in an intermediate state.
recommendedActions: Wait for the next settlement window (usually 4-6 hours)
Contact the acquiring bank to manually initiate settlement
Verify the payment status via gateway dashboard before retrying
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates T+1 settlement for UPI and card transactions

patterns.description: The issuing bank's server is temporarily unreachable or experiencing an outage.
patterns.rootCause: The bank's core banking system (CBS) is down for maintenance or experiencing technical issues. Indian banks commonly have scheduled maintenance windows between 11:30 PM - 2:00 AM IST.
recommendedActions: Route the transaction through an alternate gateway that uses a different acquiring bank
If the customer's bank is known to be down, suggest using a different payment method
Retry after 15 minutes if the issue appears transient

patterns.description: The payment gateway failed to route the transaction to the correct acquiring bank or processor.
patterns.rootCause: Internal routing logic within the gateway failed due to misconfigured merchant settings, unsupported BIN range, or missing routing rules for the payment method.
recommendedActions: Switch to an alternate gateway immediately
If using smart routing, fallback to direct integration
Escalate to gateway technical support if the error persists

patterns.description: A timeout occurred in the communication chain between payment systems (gateway → acquirer → issuer).
patterns.rootCause: The multi-hop communication between systems exceeded the timeout threshold. Each hop (merchant → gateway → processor → acquirer → issuer) adds latency, and any single slow link can cause the entire chain to timeout.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — the timeout is often transient
If retry fails, try a gateway with fewer hops in the processing chain
Check status of intermediate systems before further retries

patterns.description: The customer failed 3D Secure (Visa Secure / Mastercard SecureCode) authentication during the checkout process.
patterns.rootCause: The customer could not complete the 3DS challenge — either they entered the wrong OTP, closed the authentication popup, or the bank's 3DS server was unresponsive. 3DS is mandatory for Indian card transactions per RBI mandate.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — redirect customer to payment page again
Send helpful nudge explaining the OTP/authentication step
Offer UPI as an alternate (simpler authentication flow)
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA) for all domestic card-not-present transactions

patterns.description: The customer did not enter the OTP within the allowed time window, causing the authentication to expire.
patterns.rootCause: Indian banks typically allow 3-5 minutes for OTP entry. The customer may have experienced delayed OTP delivery (common with certain carriers like BSNL/MTNL) or simply got distracted.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — present the checkout page again for fresh OTP
Send nudge: 'Your OTP may have been delayed. Please try again.'
Suggest UPI or net banking as alternatives with different auth flows
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates AFA (OTP/biometric) for all online card transactions in India

patterns.description: The customer entered an incorrect PIN during the debit card transaction authentication.
patterns.rootCause: The PIN entered by the customer does not match the one registered with the issuing bank. After 3 incorrect attempts, most banks will block the card temporarily.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry with PIN — suggest customer verify their PIN first
Offer credit card or UPI as alternate methods (no PIN required for online)
Send helpful nudge about PIN reset options via bank app

patterns.description: The customer's card is not enrolled in the 3D Secure program, preventing the transaction from completing.
patterns.rootCause: The card has not been registered for 3D Secure / VBV / MSC by the issuing bank. Some older cards or cards issued in certain regions may not have 3DS enabled by default.
recommendedActions: Redirect customer to retry immediately with the same card (some banks auto-enroll)
Suggest the customer contact their bank to enroll in 3D Secure
Offer UPI or net banking as immediate alternatives
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates AFA for all CNP transactions — 3DS enrollment is required

patterns.description: The biometric authentication (fingerprint or face recognition) for the transaction failed on the customer's device.
patterns.rootCause: The customer's device-level biometric check (used by some UPI apps and digital wallets) did not validate successfully. Could be due to wet fingers, poor lighting for face ID, or sensor malfunction.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — biometric failures are usually one-off
Suggest customer use PIN/pattern as a fallback authentication method
Offer alternate payment method that doesn't require biometrics

patterns.description: The OTP entered by the customer does not match the one sent by the issuing bank.
patterns.rootCause: The customer may have entered an old OTP (from a previous attempt), misread the SMS, or a different OTP was received for a parallel transaction. Banks typically allow 3 attempts before blocking.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry immediately — wait for old OTP to expire
Send nudge asking customer to check for the latest SMS and try again
Suggest UPI or net banking as alternatives with simpler auth

patterns.description: The bank's authentication challenge window expired before the customer could complete the verification step.
patterns.rootCause: The bank's challenge flow (3DS 2.0 step-up authentication) has a configurable timeout (usually 5-10 minutes). The customer did not complete the challenge within this window, possibly due to page navigation or distraction.
recommendedActions: Wait 1 hour for the customer's session to fully clear
Send a cart recovery nudge with a direct checkout link
Simplify the checkout flow to reduce authentication friction

patterns.description: The customer navigated away from the checkout page without completing the payment.
patterns.rootCause: The customer dropped off during the payment flow. Common causes include: comparison shopping, unexpected total amount (shipping/taxes), too many form fields, or lack of preferred payment method.
recommendedActions: Send cart abandonment nudge within 1 hour while intent is still warm
Offer a small incentive (5-10% discount or free shipping) in the recovery message
Implement one-click checkout and saved payment methods to reduce friction

patterns.description: The payment page crashed or became unresponsive during the checkout process.
patterns.rootCause: Client-side JavaScript error, gateway SDK loading failure, or browser compatibility issue caused the checkout page to crash. More common on older Android devices with limited RAM.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — redirect customer to a fresh checkout page
Fall back to server-side payment link if client-side SDK keeps failing
Log the crash details for frontend debugging

patterns.description: The customer's preferred payment method is temporarily unavailable on the payment gateway.
patterns.rootCause: The specific payment method (e.g., HDFC net banking, or a particular UPI app) is experiencing downtime or has been disabled by the gateway for maintenance.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately with an alternate payment method displayed prominently
Switch to a backup gateway that supports the preferred method
Show real-time payment method availability status on the checkout page

patterns.description: The customer's payment session expired before they could complete the transaction.
patterns.rootCause: Payment sessions typically have a 15-30 minute timeout. If the customer takes too long to enter details or gets distracted, the session token becomes invalid and the gateway rejects the request.
recommendedActions: Redirect customer to a fresh checkout page immediately
Implement session extension with a 'Still there?' prompt
Send recovery nudge with a direct, pre-filled checkout link

patterns.description: The customer pressed the browser's back button during the payment flow, interrupting the transaction.
patterns.rootCause: Navigating backward during payment processing can break the transaction flow, especially during 3DS authentication or UPI intent redirects. The payment state becomes inconsistent.
recommendedActions: Wait 1 hour and send a cart recovery nudge
Implement browser back-button interception with a confirmation dialog
Use a modal-based checkout flow instead of page redirects

patterns.description: The checkout page took too long to load, causing the customer to abandon the payment.
patterns.rootCause: Slow network connection (2G/3G in rural India), heavy page assets, or unoptimized gateway SDK caused the checkout to take more than 5 seconds to render. Studies show 53% of mobile users abandon after 3 seconds.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately with a lighter checkout page
Implement lazy loading and CDN delivery for checkout assets
Offer a payment link via SMS as a lightweight alternative

patterns.description: The customer's coupon or promo code was invalid or expired, causing them to abandon the purchase.
patterns.rootCause: The customer attempted to apply a promotional code that was either expired, already used, or not applicable to their cart. The price increase from losing the discount caused checkout abandonment.
recommendedActions: Retry immediately — offer an alternative valid coupon code
Send a personalized recovery nudge with a fresh discount code
Show clear error messages about coupon validity before the payment step

patterns.description: Multiple rapid transactions from the same card or customer triggered the velocity fraud check.
patterns.rootCause: The gateway or bank detected too many transaction attempts in a short period (e.g., 5+ attempts within 10 minutes). This is a common fraud detection mechanism to prevent card testing attacks.
recommendedActions: Wait at least 4 hours before the next retry attempt
Do NOT attempt rapid retries — it will further increase the risk score
Send customer a message explaining the temporary hold and ask them to retry later

patterns.description: The billing address provided does not match the address on file with the card issuing bank.
patterns.rootCause: AVS (Address Verification System) check failed. The street address or postal code provided during checkout doesn't match the cardholder's registered address. Less common in India where AVS adoption is lower.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry with the same address
Send customer a nudge to verify and update their billing address
Suggest UPI payment which doesn't require address verification

patterns.description: The CVV/CVC security code entered does not match the one printed on the card.
patterns.rootCause: The 3-digit (or 4-digit for Amex) security code entered by the customer is incorrect. This is a strong fraud indicator as the CVV should only be known to the physical cardholder.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry automatically — potential fraud indicator
Show clear error asking customer to verify the CVV on their physical card
Suggest alternate payment method if customer cannot locate CVV

patterns.description: The customer's IP address location doesn't match the card's issuing country or expected region.
patterns.rootCause: The payment gateway's fraud engine detected that the customer is browsing from a different country/region than where the card was issued. Could be a legitimate traveler or VPN user, but also a common fraud pattern.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry automatically
If customer is a known repeat buyer, whitelist them
Send verification email/SMS before allowing retry

patterns.description: The customer's device fingerprint matches known patterns associated with fraudulent activity.
patterns.rootCause: Device fingerprinting detected suspicious characteristics: emulated browser, privacy-mode user agent, known bot signatures, or a device linked to previous fraud attempts in the gateway's database.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry — high fraud probability
Escalate to manual review if high-value transaction
Block the device fingerprint if pattern repeats

patterns.description: An identical transaction (same amount, card, merchant) was detected within a very short time window.
patterns.rootCause: The gateway's deduplication engine flagged this as a potential duplicate charge. Could be caused by the customer double-clicking the pay button, browser refresh during processing, or a genuine duplicate submission.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry — verify if the first transaction actually succeeded
Check the original transaction status via gateway API
If first transaction succeeded, show success page; if not, allow a fresh attempt

patterns.description: The transaction was declined because the merchant's business category (MCC) is flagged as high-risk by the issuing bank.
patterns.rootCause: Certain Merchant Category Codes (MCCs) like gaming, crypto, or adult content are blocked by some Indian banks. The issuing bank refuses transactions to these merchant categories regardless of card validity.
recommendedActions: Wait 4 hours and retry — some banks have time-based restrictions
Suggest alternate payment methods that bypass MCC checks (UPI, wallets)
Contact the acquiring bank about MCC reclassification if applicable

patterns.description: The customer has revoked the recurring payment mandate/authorization with their bank.
patterns.rootCause: The customer actively canceled the e-mandate through their banking app or by contacting their bank. The bank will reject all future auto-debit attempts on this mandate.
recommendedActions: Do NOT retry auto-debit — the mandate is permanently cancelled
Send customer a subscription renewal link for manual payment
Offer to set up a new mandate if the customer wishes to continue
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI e-mandate framework requires explicit customer consent for each mandate registration

patterns.description: The recurring payment mandate has reached its expiry date and is no longer valid.
patterns.rootCause: E-mandates in India have a defined validity period (set during registration). Once expired, the bank will reject all auto-debit requests until a new mandate is registered.
recommendedActions: Send customer a mandate renewal request via email/SMS
Provide a seamless in-app flow for new mandate registration
Process the current payment manually via a payment link
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates pre-debit notification 24 hours before each auto-debit

patterns.description: The customer has temporarily paused their subscription, blocking auto-debit charges.
patterns.rootCause: The customer used the merchant's app or the bank's interface to pause recurring charges. The mandate is still active but in a suspended state.
recommendedActions: Do NOT auto-retry — respect the customer's pause request
Send a re-engagement email after the pause period ends
Offer incentive to resume subscription (discount, free trial extension)

patterns.description: The recurring payment amount exceeds the maximum auto-debit limit set by the customer or mandated by RBI.
patterns.rootCause: RBI caps auto-debit without additional authentication at ₹15,000 per transaction. If the subscription amount exceeds this limit, the bank requires re-authentication for each charge.
recommendedActions: Wait 24 hours for limit reset, then retry with additional authentication
Send payment link for manual one-time payment above the limit
Consider splitting the charge into smaller amounts below ₹15,000
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI mandates AFA for auto-debit transactions exceeding ₹15,000

patterns.description: No valid e-mandate or auto-debit registration exists for this customer-merchant combination.
patterns.rootCause: The merchant attempted to charge the customer via auto-debit, but no mandate was registered (or the original mandate was not properly activated via the bank's validation flow).
recommendedActions: Send customer a mandate registration link
Process the current payment manually via a payment link
Verify mandate status with the payment gateway before future attempts
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI e-mandate framework requires OTP-based validation for mandate registration

patterns.description: The electronic NACH (National Automated Clearing House) debit request was rejected by the customer's bank.
patterns.rootCause: The e-NACH debit failed at the NPCI clearing level. Could be due to insufficient funds, account closure, or the bank's internal processing window mismatch. e-NACH typically processes in T+1 batches.
recommendedActions: Wait 24 hours and retry via the next NACH batch cycle
Send customer a payment link as immediate fallback
Verify the customer's bank account status before retrying
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI Circular CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-516 — maximum 3 auto-debit retry attempts within 24 hours

patterns.description: The customer's UPI autopay mandate was declined by their UPI app or linked bank.
patterns.rootCause: UPI autopay (UPI 2.0 mandate) was declined — either the customer revoked it via their UPI app, the linked bank account has insufficient funds, or the UPI app itself is experiencing issues.
recommendedActions: Wait 24 hours for the next UPI autopay cycle
Send payment link via SMS for manual UPI payment
If funds are the issue, suggest the customer add money and retry
patterns.rbiGuideline: NPCI UPI 2.0 recurring mandate guidelines — pre-debit notification required 24h before

patterns.description: The tokenized card stored for recurring payments has expired and can no longer be used for charges.
patterns.rootCause: Per RBI's Card-on-File (CoF) tokenization mandate, card tokens have a validity period tied to the underlying card's expiry. When the physical card expires, the token also becomes invalid.
recommendedActions: Send customer a notification to update their saved card details
Provide a direct link to the payment method management page
Offer UPI autopay as a token-free recurring alternative
patterns.rbiGuideline: RBI Card-on-File Tokenization guidelines (2022) — tokens are linked to card validity period
